correctness.rationale: The definition quantifies all binary scattered subsequences of each one-indexed paperfolding prefix. A greedy earliest-match proof identifies U with arch count. The odd-part rule yields B_t=001(t mod2)011p_(t+1), and an exhaustive symbolic two-state transition check gives increment 3+q-z and outgoing z, implying U(8T)=3T-p_T. All eight initial-fragment cases then yield U(8T+r) for every T and r. The residual frequency follows from the elementary exact recurrence for ones in paperfolding. The independently executed standalone verifier checks 8 whole transitions, 64 partial cases, direct prefixes to 524288 and defining predicate through N=29; finite checks do not substitute for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem determines a natural, fully quantified scattered-subsequence coverage invariant for every prefix of a canonical automatic word. Beyond pointwise exactness, it yields sharp all-N discrepancy, dyadic scaling and the entire limiting ten-point discrepancy law. These sequence-specific structural facts are not formal restatements of finite-word arch algorithms and can serve as exact benchmarks for morphic-word subword universality.
